LESSON: BUDGETING IN BUSINESS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: BUSINESS STUDIES
Strand: Business and Money Management
Topic 1.3: Budgeting in Business
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Budgeting in Business, part of Business and Money Management in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 BUSINESS STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: how to budget for emergency measures and present in class. Why is it important to prepare a budget?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the importance of budgeting in business,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Budgeting in Business in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse the types of business budgets for financial planning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Budgeting in Business in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. prepare a budget to control spending in business,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Budgeting in Business in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the need for budgeting in business. ● guide learners to brainstorm and present on the meaning and importance of budgeting, ● learners use digital devices with assistive technology or appropriate print media to search for and present on the types of business budgets, ● learners are guided to create and present a business budget, ● in pairs, learners are guided to discuss how to budget for emergency measures and present in class. Why is it important to prepare a budget?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Budgeting in Business in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain the importance of budgeting in business,

   Budgeting in Business helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. analyse the types of business budgets for financial planning,

   Budgeting in Business helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. prepare a budget to control spending in business,

   Budgeting in Business helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the need for budgeting in business. ● guide learners to brainstorm and present on the meaning and importance of budgeting, ● learners use digital devices with assistive technology or appropriate print media to search for and present on the types of business budgets, ● learners are guided to create and present a business budget, ● in pairs, learners are guided to discuss how to budget for emergency measures and present in class. Why is it important to prepare a budget?

   Budgeting in Business helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Budgeting in Business together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: learner enhances planning skills when creating and presenting a business budget.

9

● Digital literacy: learner perfects skills of interacting and connecting with digital devices with assistive technology

when using digital devices with assistive technology to search and present on the types of business budgets.

● Creativity and Imagination: learners develop networking skills when creating and presenting a business budget.

Values:
● Unity: learner works with other members of the team when brainstorming and presenting on the meaning and

importance of budgeting.

● Respect: Learner shows regard for the input of every member of the team as they brainstorm and present on the

meaning and importance of budgeting.

● Integrity: learner enhances discipline, transparency and accountability when creating a business budget.

● Love: learner respects others when brainstorming and presenting on the meaning and importance of budgeting.

● Social justice: learner exercises equity as they accord privileges without favour when sharing digital devices with

assistive technology or print or braille media to search and present on the types of business budgets.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Financial Literacy: learner enhances budgeting skills when creating a business budget.

● Internet Safety and Security: responsible online behaviour is enhanced as learners use digital devices with assistive

technology to search for information on the types of business budgets.

● Social Cohesion: learner enhances interpersonal relationships when brainstorming and presenting on the meaning

and importance of budgeting.
